newsitem.title: CANADA: StatsCan canola stocks report seen bullish - trade.
newsitem.headline: StatsCan canola stocks report seen bullish - trade.

text.p: Winnipeg Commodity Exchange canola futures were expected to open lower following projected declines in Chicago Board of Trade soy complex futures, despite tight canola stocks indicated by Statistics Canada, analysts said.
Canola futures were seen opening C$0.50 to C$1.00 a tonne lower, several analysts said. But the declines in Winnipeg were seen as less severe than the drop expected in CBOT soy.
"We'll be firmer, relative to the U.S. You can temper the bullishness of the report on a sharp drop in the U.S. market expected right off the opening," LFG analyst Rob Diziak said.
As of December 31, 1996, on-farm stocks of canola were down 20.3 percent at 2.758 million tonnes, compared with 3.460 million the previous year, the StatsCan report showed.
"It looks like the crop was overestimated. Does the report take into account grain that's sitting out in the field? Probably not," Dzisiak added.
Four percent of Prairie fields, about two million acres, had yet to be combined after a cold, wet harvest last fall, Agriculture Canada has said.

Flaxseed was seen as neutral to WCE futures, with on-farm stocks down 16.8 percent at 475,000 tonnes compared with 565,000 tonnes Dec 31, 1995. However, lower U.S. soybean calls were expected to weigh on the WCE flax market, analysts said.

"I don't see any surprises in this report. The oat number's a little lower, the farmer's still in major ownership of feed wheat and barley which is negative longer term," Pool Commodity Trading Service analyst Keith Ferley said.
Feed wheat and barley were both expected to open C$0.50 to C$1.00 per tonne lower while oats and feed peas were called steady, the analysts concurred.
